pezzi.52: I design, build and secure AI agent systems.
pezzi.53: Systems that work on real processes and stay in service over time.
pezzi.57: The models and tools I use every day. The choice is made on the single step’s objective, not out of habit: something new comes out every week, and the comparison has to be done again.
pezzi.72: My trade is not using the models. It is making them work together.
pezzi.73: I have worked with language models since before they became a mass-market product, and I have tested them as they came out ever since: today I keep sixteen configurations under comparison, from seven different providers, and I switch when the numbers justify it.
pezzi.74: I design and build agent systems: from the first line to maintenance. I connect them to the company’s data and tools, I close them inside security boundaries that do not depend on the good will of the model, and I keep them in service over time. I work both with cloud models and with models that run locally, when the data must not leave the building.
pezzi.76: Giving agents tools, limits and a way to prove what they say.
pezzi.78: Systems that stay on and have to work even when I am not watching them.
pezzi.80: The third month, not the day of the demonstration.
pezzi.81: What I have built, and what I keep in service
pezzi.82: Specialised agents in service every day, each with permissions of its own
pezzi.83: MCP servers written by me: the agent sees the operations I declare to it, not the data store
pezzi.84: Model configurations under comparison, read again on 21 August 2026
pezzi.85: Systems that stay on, and that someone has to maintain
pezzi.87: A model answers. An agent works.
pezzi.88: It takes an objective, chooses which operations to call, checks the result and stops when it is done or when it cannot go further.
pezzi.90: Can you list the unpaid invoices?

pezzi.104: Total 4 invoices pending. Note: 2026-013 (Gialli Design Studio) shows as overdue on 21 August 2026. If you also want the invoices already overdue and unpaid, tell me and I will check those separately.
pezzi.105: Every number goes back to a declared read. If the read doesn’t succeed, the agent says so instead of estimating.
pezzi.107: Not three things. One whole trade: building the system, closing it, connecting it to the data and keeping it standing.
pezzi.108: Agents from scratch: open the page
pezzi.110: I design and build both the agent and the agent’s boundary: objective, available operations, verification criteria.
pezzi.113: Several specialised agents that split the work and check one another. The one that executes is not the one that verifies.
pezzi.114: Tools and databases: open the page
pezzi.116: I connect the agents to the data and the programs the company’s already using, with operations written one by one.
pezzi.119: I build and maintain the servers that expose those operations to the agents, with the permissions of whoever calls them.
pezzi.122: Permissions live in the database and in the operating system. Five levels, and the most fragile one is the layer of instructions.
pezzi.123: Deterministic answers on data: open the page
pezzi.125: The model does not touch the data: it chooses among operations already written. Three outcomes, never confused.
pezzi.128: Choice of the parameter class, quantisation, fine-tuning on data from the client. Nothing leaves the machine.
pezzi.129: Automations and workflows: open the page
pezzi.131: What is repetitive and verifiable gets automated: where judgement is needed, a person stays.
pezzi.132: Maintenance and verification: open the page
pezzi.134: Periodic checks, regression tests, updating the models when the numbers move.
pezzi.137: From the strongest to the most fragile. The last one guarantees nothing.
pezzi.144: The rule that is not up for negotiation
pezzi.145: If a prohibition lives only in the instructions to the model, for the client it does not exist.
pezzi.148: Confusing the last two is the flaw that makes numbers get invented.
pezzi.153: It arrives as it is written in the data store, comparable with what was read.
pezzi.155: Declared absent. Not reconstructed, not estimated, not rounded.
pezzi.157: A visible error, never a plausible answer in place of a true one.
pezzi.160: Desktop application that removes personal data before the text reaches a model, and puts it back into the answer. Tuned for Italian. Runs locally.

pezzi.176: Agents that publish, flows that take away the repetitive work
pezzi.177: What is repetitive and verifiable gets automated: where judgement is needed, a person stays.
pezzi.179: Steps that repeat always in the same way
pezzi.181: Anything for which there is a way to check the outcome
pezzi.183: The exceptions nobody has written down
pezzi.184: The decisions where judgement is needed
pezzi.185: Watching over what runs on its own
pezzi.187: The deterministic part before the model.
pezzi.188: Nothing is declared done without a test.
pezzi.189: Better a visible error than a plausible, wrong answer.
pezzi.190: Every agent has only the permissions it needs.
pezzi.191: Client data stays with the client.
pezzi.192: A system counts if it stays standing over time, not on the day of the demo.
